title: Data Governance Analyst
summary: A data governance analyst makes sure a company's important data is defined, owned and trustworthy, by keeping a business glossary (agreed definitions), a data catalog and data quality checks. They sit in a data office or data management team, often in banks and large companies, and work between business data owners and the technical data teams.
dailyDuties: Add and update terms in the business glossary with data owners
Write and run data quality rules on critical data elements
Publish data quality scorecards and follow up on failed checks
Map data lineage from source systems to reports
Run catalog updates in Collibra, Alation or Microsoft Purview
Meet data stewards to agree definitions and fix issues
Prepare governance updates for the data governance council

skills.expectation: Maintain data ownership, stewardship, lineage and critical data elements under a governance framework such as DAMA-DMBOK
Write data quality rules, profile data and publish data quality scorecards
Keep the business glossary and catalog current in Collibra, Alation or Microsoft Purview
Write SQL to profile data, test quality rules and trace lineage
Read data models to find where critical data elements live and how they flow
Work with data owners and stewards across business teams to agree definitions and fixes
Write clear definitions, policies and governance updates for non-technical teams
Tag personal data and support DPDP Act or GDPR requirements
Automate data quality checks with Python or PySpark
Build governance and data quality dashboards
Know banking rules such as BCBS 239 and regulatory reporting
Understand data pipelines well enough to map lineage across them

certifications.why: Microsoft compliance basics, including Purview, for Purview-based teams
Indian privacy credential for roles that also handle DPDP tagging
